content.title: About
content.content: Cheese sauce is a thick, flavorful sauce made from processed cheese, milk, and seasonings. It is commonly used as a topping for french fries, chicken nuggets, vegetables, and pasta dishes. The taste combines the creamy richness of cheese with a mild tang and aromatic spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese sauce originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a quick way to add a cheesy flavor to fast‑food items.
Emulsifiers such as mono‑ and diglycerides are often added to achieve a smooth texture.
There are many variations, including versions with chili, garlic, smoked cheese, or herbs.
In fast‑food restaurants the sauce is frequently served in small plastic packets.
In some countries the sauce is classified as a ready‑to‑heat product.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese sauce provides calcium, which is essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: It supplies a modest amount of protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sauce contains vitamins B2 and B12, which help with energy metabolism.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and contribute to satiety.

items.title: Enhances palatability
items.content: Cheese sauce makes foods more appealing, which can encourage a more varied diet.

items.title: High in fat and calories
items.content: Cheese sauce is calorie‑dense and contains saturated fats, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: It contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for those with intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk or cheese may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The sauce can be high in sodium, which is a concern for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cheese sauce warm with french fries, chicken nuggets, vegetable sticks, over pasta, in burritos, or as a base for casseroles. Heat it in the microwave or on the stovetop, stirring constantly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce refrigerated at 2 °C–5 °C. After opening, use within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: Bottled or canned coffee is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from brewed coffee extract, often sweetened and flavored with milk, sugar, or stabilizers. It is sealed in airtight containers, allowing it to stay fresh for months without losing aroma or taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑drink coffee in a bottle appeared in Japan in the 1970s.
In the United States, canned coffee popularity surged after Starbucks launched its Frappuccino line in the 1990s.
Bottled coffee is usually pasteurized, extending shelf life up to 12 months.
A wide range of flavors exists, from classic espresso to caramel latte and vanilla macchiato.
Aluminum cans better preserve flavor than glass because they protect the drink from light.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Boosts alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, improving concentration and reducing fatigue.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption has been linked to a slight increase in metabolic rate and fat oxidation.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate coffee intake is associated with reduced risk of Parkinson’s disease, type‑2 diabetes, and some cancers.

items.title: Improves mood
items.content: Caffeine raises dopamine and serotonin levels, which can enhance mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat when consuming too much coffee.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened ready‑to‑drink coffees can contain high amounts of sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or weight management.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee’s natural acidity may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or acid reflux.

items.title: Additives and preservatives
items.content: Certain brands use artificial flavors, stabilizers, and preservatives that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The drink can be enjoyed cold straight from the bottle or can, or poured over ice. It can be diluted with water, mixed with milk, cream, or a sweetener. It pairs well with desserts, pastries, and breakfast items.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bottles and cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the product refrigerated, tightly sealed, and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: White fish, mixed species, grilled, is a tender and flavorful product made from several types of white-fleshed marine fish. Grilling preserves the natural taste while giving the surface a light, crispy crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix often includes cod, pollock, sea bass, and hake.
Grilling enhances aroma through the caramelization of proteins and fats.
White fish is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are heart‑healthy.
In some countries the grilled white‑fish mix is a traditional summer dish.
When properly cooked, the fish stays juicy and does not dry out.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: White fish provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health and help reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, vital for thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with fatty fish, white fish has moderate fat content, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory issues.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain marine species can accumulate mercury and other toxins; varying sources is recommended.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions may cause stomach discomfort in people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fish as a main dish, slice it for salads, use in sandwiches, or add to pasta. Pair with lemon, olive oil, fresh herbs, and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the fish refrigerated at 0 °C–2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C and thaw in the fridge before use.

content.title: About
content.content: Ground meat NFS is finely minced meat (commonly beef, pork, or a blend) without added preservatives or flavorings. It is intended for culinary use in dishes that require quick, even cooking of meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground meat is a staple in many traditional dishes worldwide: burgers, meatballs, sauces, and fillings.
When properly minced, the meat retains most of the nutrients of the original cuts.
In the US, NFS (Not From Specified) indicates the product is not tied to a specific cut but is a mixture.
Ground meat can be made from various parts of the animal – neck, shoulder, or thigh – affecting flavor and fat content.
A small amount of ice or cold water is sometimes added to improve texture.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground meat provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Heme iron from meat is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The fine texture speeds up digestion compared with whole cuts of meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Ground meat spoils quickly; keep it at 4 °C or below and cook it thoroughly.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Depending on the cuts used, ground meat can be fatty; choose lean versions if monitoring calories.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific types of meat.

items.title: Additive presence
items.content: Some manufacturers add stabilizers or flavor enhancers—check the label if you have dietary restrictions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ground meat is suitable for frying, stewing, baking, and boiling. Form it into patties, use in sauces, stuff vegetables, make meatballs, dumplings, or casseroles. For a softer texture, mix in a little cold water or ice before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground meat in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw completely in the fridge before use and cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.
